title: Quantum Field Attenuation Scaler
description: In a physics simulation lab, you need to compute the scaling factor of a quantum field over time. Given a floating-point base amplitude 'base' and an integer exponent 'steps', write a function to calculate base raised to the power steps (i.e., base^steps). The exponent can be negative, zero, or positive.
input_format: A double representing the base amplitude and an integer representing the exponent steps.
output_format: A double representing the calculated field scaling factor.

examples.explanation: 2 raised to the power of 10 is 1024.
2.1 raised to the power of 3 is approximately 9.261.
